formal_answer.question: Does homodimer sequence self-co-occurrence rescue the interface blindspot, or is the failure architectural across all three classes?
formal_answer.conclusion: Homodimer sequence self-co-occurrence does NOT rescue the quaternary interface blindspot. In Class 1 (Homooligomer, p53), the raw correlation with binding is strongly negative (rho = -0.446) and the partial correlation remains inverted (rho = -0.354, three-way beta = -0.7929). The failure is architectural across all three evolutionary classes: single-chain masked language model objectives enforce monomeric stability priors that systematically penalize quaternary interface adaptations.

overall_conclusion: Single-chain protein language models fail decisively at quaternary protein-protein interfaces across all 3 evolutionary classes. Sequence self-co-occurrence in homooligomers (p53) does NOT rescue the blindspot (rho_partial = -0.365, PLM:Binding:Interface beta = -0.883, p < 1e-15). Natural heterodimers (HLA-A2, GB1) exhibit apparent binding correlations that are over 60-80% mediated by monomer expression/folding. Synthetic and de novo binders (KRAS-DARPin, Spike RBD-ACE2) show complete absence of binding sensitivity. The quaternary interface failure is fundamental and architectural.
